q: How much mine methane comes with coking coal from Karaganda underground mines?
title: Karaganda coking coal: mine methane
short: Karaganda coking coal comes from deep underground mines, which release far more methane than open pits. Without mine data, IPCC Tier 1 gives 18 cubic metres per tonne, with a range of 10 to 25, plus about 2.5 after mining. Ask for ventilation measurements.
audience: Steel plants and coke makers buying coking coal from the Karaganda basin

ul: Underground mining: 10 to 25 cubic metres per tonne, 18 average (IPCC 2006).
Post mining: about 2.5 cubic metres per tonne.
One cubic metre weighs about 0.67 kg.

p: Gassy mines monitor ventilation air and degasification. A figure from those records is more accurate than the default.
Scope 3 for a steel plant buying the coal. Scope 1 if your group runs the mine, as some integrated steel groups do.
